extracted.intended_audience: state agencies, rule drafters, administrative law practitioners, regulated persons, and stakeholders participating in Florida rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for adopting, publishing, challenging, and reviewing administrative rules in Florida under the Florida Administrative Procedure Act (Ch. 120). Covers emergency rules, uniform rules, federal-identical rules, petitions to initiate rulemaking, rulemaking records, estimated regulatory cost statements, variances/waivers, and agency review of rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency rule authority and triggering conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may adopt emergency rules if it finds an immediate danger to the public health, safety, or welfare requires emergency action or if the Legislature authorizes adoption and finds the specified conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption must be within the agency's constitutional or delegated authority. The agency may adopt any rule necessitated by the immediate danger or legislative finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural fairness for emergency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may adopt an emergency rule by any procedure which is fair under the circumstances, provided the procedure offers at least the procedural protection given by other statutes, the State Constitution, or the U.S. Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must ensure emergency procedures meet baseline constitutional and statutory procedural protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation for emergency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An emergency rule must take only that action necessary to protect the public interest under the emergency procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should limit emergency rules to the minimum measures required by the emergency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and findings for emergency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of or prior to action, the agency must publish in writing the specific facts and reasons for finding an immediate danger and reasons for concluding the procedure used is fair; notice (including full text and findings) must be published in the Florida Administrative Register (FAR) except for certain local units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency's findings of immediate danger, necessity, and procedural fairness are judicially reviewable; provide incorporated materials to the oversight committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter examples for emergency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency rules pertaining to public health, safety, or welfare include rules for perishable agricultural commodities and interpretation/implementation of election code chapters 97-102 and 105.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute lists these subject matters as examples that fall within emergency rule authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency rule duration limit (90 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: An emergency rule may not be effective for longer than 90 days and may not be renewable except under limited conditions where the agency has initiated rulemaking and either a challenge to the proposed rules is pending or the proposed rules are awaiting ratification by the Legislature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the proposed rule is not ratified during the next regular session, the emergency rule expires at adjournment sine die; proposed rules must be withdrawn from ratification per s.120.541(3)(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency rule renewal publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of renewal of an emergency rule must be published in the FAR before expiration and must state the specific facts and reasons for renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal requires explanation of continued necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: History note requirement for long emergency rules replacing existing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For emergency rules with effective period >90 days intended to replace existing rules, a history note must be added to the existing rule specifically identifying the emergency rule and the filing date with the Department of State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures traceability when emergency rules supplant existing rules for extended periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of emergency rules in Florida Administrative Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency rules must be published in the Florida Administrative Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow normal publication channels so emergency rules are part of codified materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superseding emergency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may supersede an existing emergency rule by adopting another emergency rule before the first expires; reason for adopting the superseding rule must be stated in accordance with the procedural-fairness publication requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A superseding emergency rule may not be in effect longer than the duration of the superseded rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical corrections to emergency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may make technical changes to an emergency rule within the first 7 days after adoption; such changes must be published in the FAR as a notice of correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical changes are limited to a 7-day window and require formal correction notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date for emergency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to constitutional/statutory provisions, an emergency rule becomes effective immediately on filing, or on a date less than 20 days thereafter if specified, if the agency finds such date necessary because of immediate danger to public health, safety, or welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows immediate effect when necessary to address imminent threats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal of emergency rules prior to expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may repeal an emergency rule before it expires by providing notice of intended action in the FAR, including full text, a summary, reference to rule number if applicable, and a short plain explanation why conditions no longer require the emergency rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides transparency and rationale when rescinding emergency measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration Commission adoption of uniform rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administration Commission shall adopt one or more sets of uniform rules of procedure (to be reviewed by the committee and filed with Department of State); agencies must comply by specified dates unless exceptions are granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform rules establish baseline procedures for agencies subject to Ch. 120; filing makes them agency procedures unless exceptions are approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to uniform rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may seek exceptions to uniform rules by petitioning the Administration Commission; exceptions may be approved to implement other statutes, conform to federal-funding conditions or to permit tax benefits, or as required for efficient agency operation; reasons for exceptions must be published in the FAR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process ensures exceptions are limited and publicly documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate chapter for agency exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies with approved exceptions shall publish a separate chapter in the Florida Administrative Code delineating the provisions that provide exceptions and specifying each alternative chosen from uniform rules; chapters must be organized like the uniform rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a uniform way to identify agency deviations from standard procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform rules requirement: scheduling public meetings/hearings/workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform rules must include rules for scheduling public meetings, hearings, and workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardize scheduling procedures across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform rules for communications media technology hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform rules must provide procedures for conducting meetings/hearings/workshops in person and by communications media technology, requiring equal consideration of all evidence/testimony regardless of communication method, specifying notice content and locations for access, and preserving public records inspection rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'communications media technology' broadly (electronic transmission of printed matter, audio, video, etc.) and requires liberal construction of public meeting laws to apply to remote formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform rules for filing protests and bonds
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform rules shall include procedures for filing notices of protests and formal written protests; the Administration Commission may prescribe form and bond substantive provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardizes protest procedures and bonding requirements when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of petitions for administrative hearings (petition elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform rules for filing petitions under ss.120.569 or 120.57 shall require the petition to include: (a) identification of petitioner including e-mail if any; (b) statement of when/how petitioner received notice of the agency action or proposed action; (c) explanation of how petitioner's substantial interests are or will be affected; (d) statement of all material disputed facts or that there are none; (e) a statement of the ultimate facts alleged including specific facts petitioner contends warrant reversal/modification; (f) statement of specific rules/statutes petitioner contends require reversal/modification and explanation of how facts relate; (g) statement of relief sought precisely describing desired agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must be specific and cover identity, notice receipt, standing, disputed facts, legal grounds, and requested relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents for respondent's request for administrative hearing in enforcement matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform rules shall require requests to include: (a) name, address, e-mail, phone of party and counsel/representative; (b) a statement that respondent requests a hearing and disputes material facts (identifying disputed facts) or requests hearing and does not dispute material facts; (c) reference by file number to administrative complaint and date received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may provide an election-of-rights form that must only call for this information and not impose extra requirements unless authorized by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform rules for petitions for declaratory statements and FAR notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform rules must provide procedures for filing and prompt disposition of petitions for declaratory statements and describe contents of notices to be published in the FAR under s.120.565, including time limits for petitions to intervene or for hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures consistent handling and public notice for declaratory statement petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency organization statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform rules must provide a method for each agency head to provide a description of the agency's organization and general course of operations, and require that statement to be published on the agency's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotes transparency about agency structure and functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform rules for variances and waivers procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform rules shall establish procedures for granting or denying petitions for variances and waivers under s.120.542.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes processes and standards agencies must follow when considering relief from rule requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of federal standards: notice and comment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When adopting rules substantively identical to federal regulations, the agency must publish notice of intent in the FAR at least 21 days prior to filing the rule with the Department of State, provide a copy to the committee at least 21 days prior, consider written comments received within 14 days after notice publication, and the rule is adopted upon filing (substantive changes require republishing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streamlined state adoption of federal regs requires short-notice timeline and limited comment window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date alignment for federal-identical rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule adopted pursuant to the federal-standards subsection becomes effective on the date designated by the agency but not earlier than the federal regulation's effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State rules cannot take effect before the federal effective date when adopted as substantively identical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection procedure for federal-identical rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any substantially affected person may file an objection within 14 days after publication of the notice of intent; objection must specify portions objected to and specific reasons; agency shall not proceed with portions specified unless it deems objection frivolous, but may proceed under subsection (3). An objection to a rule that does not materially differ from the federal regulation is deemed frivolous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short objection window and frivolous-objection standard constrain challenges to federal-identical adoptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to repeal or revise when federal regulation changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If a federal regulation adopted as state rule is declared invalid/withdrawn/revoked/remanded/suspended, the agency shall publish a notice of repeal in the FAR within 60 days; if federal regulation is substantially amended, agency may adopt the amendment as a rule within 180 days or else the original rule is deemed repealed and agency must publish a repeal notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires agencies to track federal changes and act within set timelines to keep state rules in sync or to repeal them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference federal regulation in rule text
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a rule proposed for adoption is substantively identical to a federal regulation, the rule shall be written to specifically reference the federal regulation whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-referencing improves clarity and demonstrates identity with federal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to petition to initiate rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person regulated by an agency or having a substantial interest in an agency rule may petition the agency to adopt, amend, or repeal a rule or to provide minimum public information required by chapter; petition must specify the proposed rule and requested action; agency must provide a copy to the committee within 7 days of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opens rulemaking initiation to regulated persons and interested stakeholders and mandates agency notification to oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency response deadlines to petitions to initiate rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than 30 calendar days following filing of a petition the agency shall initiate rulemaking, otherwise comply with requested action, or deny the petition with written reasons; the agency shall notify the committee of intended action or response within 7 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforces prompt agency action or reasoned denial on petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for petitions directed to unadopted rules (public hearing option)
rubrics_metrics.description: If petition is directed to an unadopted rule, the agency shall within 30 days initiate rulemaking or provide notice in the FAR that the agency will hold a public hearing on the petition within 30 days after publication of the notice; the public hearing considers comments on scope, application, and whether the public interest is served by case-by-case application vs. rule adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows public input before agency relies on unadopted rules; hearing narrows scope and explores alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency statement and committee hearing when no action taken after hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If agency does not initiate rulemaking or comply within 30 days after the public hearing, it shall publish in the FAR a statement of reasons for not initiating rulemaking or complying and of any changes to scope/application; file the statement with the committee, which may hold a hearing and recommend legislative action to make rule statutory or modify agency authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides oversight recourse when agencies decline action after process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of rule development and 180-day proposed rule filing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If agency initiates rulemaking after the hearing, it must publish a notice of rule development within 30 days after the hearing and file a notice of proposed rule within 180 days after the notice of rule development unless it publishes an explanation for delay before day 180.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeps momentum and limits delay in proceeding from petition/hearing to proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking record contents
rubrics_metrics.description: In all rulemaking proceedings the agency shall compile a rulemaking record that includes: all notices given for the proposed rule; any statement of estimated regulatory costs; written summary of hearings; written comments and responses as required; all notices and findings under emergency rules; all materials filed by the agency with the committee and Department of State; all written inquiries from standing legislative committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must retain the rulemaking record while the rule is in effect; when rule no longer in effect the record may be destroyed per records-retention schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of lower-cost regulatory alternative (timing and effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 21 days after publication of the s.120.54(3)(a) notice, a substantially affected person may submit a good faith written proposal for a lower cost regulatory alternative that substantially accomplishes the law's objectives; submission extends the 90-day filing period by 21 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must prepare or revise a statement of estimated regulatory costs and either adopt the alternative or state reasons for rejecting it; agency must provide copies of the proposal and its response to the committee within 7 days and cannot file the rule until those documents are provided to the committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a statement of estimated regulatory costs is required (>$200,000/1-year and $1M/5-year thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposed rule will adversely impact small business or is likely to directly/indirectly increase regulatory costs in excess of $200,000 in the aggregate within 1 year, the agency shall prepare a statement as required by s.120.54(3)(b); additionally, the statement must analyze whether the rule is likely to have adverse impacts in excess of $1 million in aggregate within 5 years on economic growth/jobs/investment, business competitiveness/productivity/innovation, or increase regulatory costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers for additional analysis and potential legislative ratification; thresholds and time windows are prescribed statutory measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revising statement of estimated regulatory costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency shall revise a statement of estimated regulatory costs if any change to the rule under s.120.54(3)(d) increases the regulatory costs of the rule; provide the revision at least 21 days before filing the rule to the person who submitted the alternative and to the committee and post notice on agency website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures stakeholders see revised cost estimates before final filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material failure and limitations on raising failure in challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure of the agency to prepare the required statement or to respond to a written lower-cost alternative is a material failure to follow rulemaking procedures; however, such failure may not be raised in a proceeding challenging rule validity unless raised in a petition filed no later than 1 year after effective date and by a person whose substantial interests are affected by the rule's regulatory costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a time and standing limitation on procedural challenges based on cost-statement omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenging a rule on rejection of lower-cost alternative (conditions to invalidate)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule challenged under s.120.52(8)(f) may not be declared invalid unless: (1) issue raised in administrative proceeding within 1 year after effective date; (2) challenge is to agency's rejection of a lower-cost regulatory alternative offered under s.120.541(1)(a) or s.120.54(3)(b)2.b.; and (3) challenger's substantial interests are materially affected by the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits judicial invalidation to particular procedural/factual circumstances tied to lower-cost alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in a statement of estimated regulatory costs (detailed elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement must include: (a) an economic analysis addressing specified $1M-in-5-years thresholds (growth, competitiveness, regulatory costs); (b) a good faith estimate of number and types of individuals/entities affected; (c) a good faith estimate of costs to agency and other government entities and effects on revenues; (d) a good faith estimate of transactional costs to regulated persons (with an enumerated list of possible transactional cost items); (e) analysis of impact on small businesses and small counties/cities and basis for rejecting alternatives to reduce impacts; (f) market impacts (changes to customer charges, market value, substitute costs, reasonable value of time to comply); (g) any additional useful information the agency determines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must provide granular cost estimates and analyses; transactional costs list is extensive (filing fees, licensing expenses, equipment, installation, operations, accounting, labor, materials, capital expenditures, professional services, monitoring/reporting, training/testing, travel, insurance/surety, allocation of overhead, reduced sales, others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement must describe alternatives and legislative ratification when thresholds met
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement or revised statement must describe any regulatory alternatives submitted and state whether the agency adopts the alternative or reasons for rejecting it; if adverse impacts exceed the 2(a) criteria, the rule must be submitted to the President of the Senate and Speaker of the House no later than 30 days before the next regular session and may not take effect until ratified by the Legislature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serious-impact rules are subject to legislative review and possible ratification requirement; agency must notify the committee within 3 business days of submission to the Legislature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and website availability of cost statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of State shall include agency website addresses on the FAR website where statements of estimated regulatory costs can be viewed; agencies must include the website address in the notice and provide it for publication; revisions must include the website address as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures public access to full cost statements through centralized indexing and proper notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules ombudsman form requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules ombudsman in the Executive Office of the Governor must prescribe and post a form that incorporates the factors in subsection (2); agencies must use this form to prepare statements of estimated regulatory costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardizes the structure of cost statements across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of variances and waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Variances and waivers provide relief where strict application of uniform rule requirements would lead to unreasonable, unfair, or unintended results; a public employee is not a 'person subject to regulation' for purposes of petitioning for variance/waiver in capacity as public employee; agencies authorized to grant variances/waivers consistent with this section but may not grant variances from statutes or federal-required rules except as allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variance/waiver scheme is supplemental and limited; agencies can impose conditions/duration only as necessary to achieve underlying statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for granting variances or waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Variances/waivers shall be granted when the person demonstrates the purpose of the underlying statute will be or has been achieved by other means and when application of a rule would create a substantial hardship or violate principles of fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Substantial hardship' includes demonstrated economic, technological, legal, or other hardship; 'principles of fairness' are violated when literal application affects a person significantly differently than similarly situated persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform rules for variances/waivers including emergency/temporary relief
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administration Commission shall adopt uniform rules of procedure for granting/denying variances and waivers, including procedures for emergency and temporary variances/waivers that may provide expedited timeframes, waiver or limited public notice, and limitations on comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows flexibility and expedited processing for temporary/emergency relief while maintaining procedural guardrails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency duty to inform about variances/waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall advise persons of remedies available through this section and provide copies of the section, the uniform rules on variances and waivers, and, if requested, the underlying statute to persons who inquire about relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must proactively inform regulated persons about relief options and procedural materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in a petition for variance or waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Each petition must specify: (a) the rule from which relief is requested; (b) the type of action requested; (c) the specific facts that justify the waiver/variance for the petitioner; (d) the reason why the requested relief would serve the purposes of the underlying statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must be factual, specific, and explain statutory fit for the requested relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and publication for petitions for variances/waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 15 days after receipt of a petition, the agency shall provide notice to the Department of State, which will publish the petition notice in the first available FAR issue; notice must contain petitioner name, filing date, rule number/nature, and how to obtain a copy; uniform rules shall provide a means for interested persons to comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates public notice and comment opportunity for variance/waiver petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency review timelines and information requests for variances/waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for emergency requests, within 30 days after receipt of a petition the agency shall review it and request additional information the agency is permitted to require; within 30 days after receipt of additional information the agency may request only clarifying information related to new questions; if petitioner asserts a request for additional info is unauthorized, the agency shall proceed at the petitioner's written request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits the scope and timing of follow-up information requests to prevent unduly delaying processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision deadline and deemed approval for variances/waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency shall grant or deny a petition within 90 days after receipt of the timely requested original petition, additional material, or the petitioner's written request to finish processing; a petition not decided within 90 days after receipt of a completed petition is deemed approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order granting/denying must be filed with committee and contain factual/reasoned support; notice of disposition published in FAR and must be supported by competent substantial evidence and is subject to ss.120.569 and 120.57 (with limited scope for proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency record-keeping for variances/waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall maintain a record of the type and disposition of each petition, including temporary and emergency variances and waivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures transparency and accountability in relief-granting practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency review of existing rules timeline (beginning provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: By July 1, 2030, each agency, in coordination with the committee, shall review all existing rules adopted by the agency before July 1, 2025, in accordance with this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section starts a systematic agency rule review requirement (full requirements appear beyond chunk).
